is recorded and the order stays flagged for manual review). It converts nothing.

Events that arrived before their payment record and are being retried within bounds (`pending`), were applied

post.description:
Needs the current password. A confirmation link goes to the NEW address and a notice to the current one; nothing changes
until the link is used. The answer does not reveal whether the new address is already taken.
(Re)sends the confirmation link to the signed-in account's address. Nothing happens if it is already verified.
Needs the current password. Signs out every other device and returns a fresh token pair for this one.
Sends a reset link if the address belongs to an active account. The answer is identical either way.
Sets a new password from an emailed link (works once). Signs the account out everywhere.

409.description: Either code=price_changed (cart prices changed; the cart is already updated, review the new total and check out again), or the Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.

503.description: Shipping/tax are not configured; checkout is disabled.

post.description:
Cancels an UNPAID (pending) order: the customer who owns it, or an administrator. The payment is made
unpayable at the provider first, then the order is cancelled and its stock restocked together.

A paid order cannot be cancelled here (409 cancellation_not_allowed): it is refunded by an administrator.
If the provider cannot confirm the payment state the order is NOT cancelled (409 cancellation_unconfirmed)
and the attempt is reconciled. Cancelling twice is safe.

Record a parcel handed to a carrier. Allowed for PAID or FULFILLED orders. Optional `fulfill_order: true` also marks a PAID order
FULFILLED. The tracking number and link may be added later.

delete.description: Remove a shipment entered by mistake (the audit log keeps a record of it).

patch.description: Correct the carrier, add or clear the tracking number or link, or mark the parcel delivered.

Administrator status change. Only `fulfilled` (from `paid`) is allowed. `paid`, `refunded` and `cancelled`
are refused (409 status_change_not_allowed) because setting them by hand would fabricate a payment, claim
an unconfirmed refund, or cancel without payment/stock handling: those go through the payment provider,
POST /payments/{order_id}/refund, and POST /orders/{order_id}/cancel.

post.description:
Creates (or reuses) a Stripe PaymentIntent for one of the caller's own
orders and returns the client secret needed to confirm it on the
client side. Always self-service: this cannot be used to start a
payment on another user's order, even by an admin.

A signed-in user pays their own orders. A GUEST pays only with the order-scoped payment capability that checkout
set in an HttpOnly cookie for that exact order (401 without any credential, 404 for a wrong or expired one).
Stripe's webhook (kept at this path for compatibility; same as /webhooks/stripe).

(inside its PaymentProvider) and signature header, never changes the shared lifecycle rules.

schema.title: Response Provider Webhook Api V1 Payments Webhooks  Provider  Post

post.description:
Admin-only. REQUESTS a refund of the order's successful payment; it does not refund anything yet.
A background job asks the payment provider (with a retry-safe idempotency key), and the order is
marked `refunded` only after the provider CONFIRMS the refund. Poll GET /admin/refunds (or the
order) for the outcome. Asking again returns the same refund.

Turn a simple product into a product with options, moving its stock onto the variants EXACTLY (allocated stock must equal the
product's current stock, and `expected_stock` must still match). Refused while an unpaid or paid-but-unshipped order contains it.
Its cart lines are removed. All or nothing.

patch.description: Rename a value. Orders already placed keep the name they were bought under.

put.description:
Define a product's option sets (up to 3, e.g. Size and Colour, each with its values). Only for a product with no variants, no stock
and no carts or orders; otherwise use convert-to-variants. An empty list makes it a simple product again.

post.description: Review a product you bought (a paid or shipped order). One review per product; edit it afterwards.
The same for a simple product. A product with options keeps its stock on its variants.

get.description: Every stock change of the product (and its variants), newest first: sales, restocks, administrators' changes, with before and after.

post.description: Up to 100 variants, all or none. Each names a value for every option, its own SKU and stock, and optionally its own price.

get.description: The combinations of the option values that have no variant yet. A convenience for choosing what to create: nothing is created.

delete.description: Only a variant that never had stock and is in no cart or order. Otherwise set it to inactive.

patch.description: Change the price override (null removes it) or the status. SKU, option values and stock cannot be changed here.

post.description: Set a variant's stock (`set_to`) or add/remove units (`delta`). A reason is required; the change is recorded with who made it.

get.description: Rating average and distribution for up to 50 products at once (for the stars on a product list). Published reviews only.
